original_abstract.text: Recommending creators that a user does not yet follow is a cold-start problem: from hundreds of thousands of popular creators and only a short trail of prior engagements, the system must predict the next creator worth surfacing. The prevailing generative recommendation recipe tokenizes each creator into a \emph{Semantic ID} (SID) by quantizing a frozen embedding and trains a language model to generate SIDs. We show that this SID layer, not the language model, is the binding constraint. The creator-to-SID map is many-to-one, so colliding creators must be resolved by a popularity tie-break that caps creator-level recall and favors already-popular creators, and the frozen quantizer stops the training gradient from reaching the creator representation. We propose Atomic Creator Token (ACT), which gives every creator its own vocabulary token trained end-to-end. The map is bijective, so collisions are impossible and inference is a direct top-$k$ over creator logits. In a controlled comparison on production data in which the token layer is the only variable, ACT improves creator-level Recall@15 by 19.8 points ($1.84\times$) over a matched SID baseline, still leads when the SID codebook is enlarged $64\times$, and serves at ${\sim}2.7\times$ lower per-user latency. The advantage carries over to the public KuaiRand dataset, where ACT is the only method that beats a global-popularity baseline, provided each creator token sees enough training examples. In a live A/B test, ACT is directionally positive on every reported metric against both the SID-enhanced and the classic production rankers.
original_abstract.source_title: Beyond Semantic IDs: Atomic Creator Tokens for Large-Scale Generative Recommendation

en.text: Atomic Creator Token assigns each creator a unique, end-to-end-trained vocabulary token instead of a frozen quantized semantic ID. A controlled production-data comparison reports a 19.8-point Recall@15 gain and about 2.7× lower per-user latency; public-data gains require enough training examples per creator, and online metrics are reported as directionally positive.

zh.text: Atomic Creator Token为每个创作者分配唯一且端到端训练的词表token，替代冻结量化的语义ID。生产数据受控对比报告Recall@15提高19.8个百分点、人均延迟约降低至原来的1/2.7；公开数据上的收益依赖每位创作者有足够训练样本，线上结果报告为方向性正向。

original_abstract.text: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) models expand model capacity by activating only a subset of experts for each token. On accelerators with static execution plans, expert capacities and placement are fixed before routing reveals each expert's load. Uniform worst-case capacities waste work on padding; smaller capacities tied to expert identities can overflow. We present RankLane, which ranks each device's experts by current load and assigns them to fixed-capacity lanes. Runtime indices select experts and token rows while tier populations, shapes and device placement remain fixed. An aggregation graph preserves device ownership and reduces each token's local contributions on one core. Routing calibration and measured execution costs guide tier selection; overflowing chunks rerun at full capacity. We evaluate full-model prefill of Qwen3-30B-A3B and Gemma 4 26B-A4B with MXFP6 weights on four Cloud AI 100 Ultra SoCs, using 128-2048-token chunks and including overflow detection and in-program recovery support. Against a dense baseline, RankLane achieves end-to-end prefill speedups of 1.27-4.18x on Qwen3 and 1.93-3.46x on Gemma.
original_abstract.source_title: RankLane: Efficient MoE Prefill on Accelerators with Ranked Expert Capacities

en.text: RankLane assigns dynamically ranked expert loads to fixed-capacity execution lanes, combining static shapes with runtime expert selection and full-capacity overflow recovery. Four Cloud AI 100 Ultra SoCs with MXFP6 weights show full-model prefill speedups of 1.27–4.18× for Qwen3-30B-A3B and 1.93–3.46× for Gemma 4 26B-A4B over the evaluated dense baseline.

zh.text: RankLane按当前负载给专家排序并分配到固定容量执行通道，在静态形状下动态选专家，并在溢出时以全容量重跑。四颗Cloud AI 100 Ultra SoC、MXFP6权重测试中，相对所测稠密执行基线，Qwen3-30B-A3B与Gemma 4 26B-A4B全模型预填充分别加速1.27—4.18倍、1.93—3.46倍。

original_abstract.text: We present WeSearch, a unified, model-centric retrieval framework for large-scale, continuously evolving content search. Prevailing methods assign documents fixed hierarchical Semantic IDs, implicitly assuming each document follows a single coherent semantic path-an assumption that often breaks down for multi-topic documents. WeSearch instead retrieves query-relevant clusters and then ranks atomic documents within the resulting query-specific candidate space, decoupling candidate pruning from fine-grained relevance modeling. Combined with relevance-aware training, compact document representations, and incremental index updates, this design enables weekly-or daily when needed-model refreshes. Deployed as the primary semantic retrieval path in WeChat Search alongside a lexical syntax tree, WeSearch shows consistent one-week A/B gains on corpora from hundreds of millions to billions of documents, and a one-month full-traffic A/B test confirms stable improvements of +0.68% CTR and +2.27% per-user article clicks, together with a 41% reduction in retrieval resource cost and a 19 ms reduction in graphic-text retrieval latency. WeSearch is now fully deployed in WeChat Search, serving 100% of production traffic.
original_abstract.source_title: WeSearch: A Unified Model-Centric Retrieval Framework for WeChat Search

en.text: WeSearch retrieves query-relevant clusters before ranking atomic documents, decoupling candidate pruning from document relevance. Compact representations and incremental updates support frequent refreshes; the authors report full deployment in WeChat Search, with a month-long test showing +0.68% CTR, +2.27% per-user article clicks, 41% lower retrieval resource cost and 19 ms lower graphic-text retrieval latency.

zh.text: WeSearch先检索与查询相关的簇，再对簇内原子文档排序，将候选裁剪与精细相关性建模分离。紧凑表示和增量索引支持频繁更新；作者报告已在微信搜索全量部署，一个月实验中CTR提升0.68%、人均文章点击提升2.27%，检索资源成本下降41%，图文检索延迟降低19毫秒。

original_abstract.text: Long-horizon reasoning and agentic workloads strain KV-cache capacity and decode attention throughput. We present Jet-QSparse, a training-free method that combines compact NVFP4 cache storage with native FP4 query-key computation on Blackwell tensor cores. A dense scan scores the full key history and selects 128-token blocks for sparse FP16 value aggregation with FP32 accumulation, preserving higher precision in the output-forming step while enabling contiguous tile loads. Calibrated key centering and at most two BF16 pages per sequence and layer address quantization error; FP8 prefill uses a temporary arena while the persistent cache is packed directly from BF16 activations. Across four hybrid LLMs, a budget of 128 blocks per KV head shows no detected accuracy loss on the evaluated mathematical reasoning, coding, and agentic benchmarks, although some smaller budgets incur losses. With 64 blocks, Qwen3.8-27B achieves a $1.94\times$ end-to-end decode speedup over dense BF16 at 128K context and batch size 16 on one GB300, and the measured Qwen KV pools provide $2.58$-$2.76\times$ BF16's token capacity.
original_abstract.source_title: Jet-QSparse: Accelerating Agentic LLM Inference with 4-Bit Sparse Attention

en.text: Jet-QSparse combines NVFP4 KV storage and native FP4 key scoring with sparse higher-precision value aggregation on Blackwell. A 128-block budget shows no detected loss on evaluated tasks; a separate 64-block setting gives Qwen3.8-27B a 1.94× decode speedup at 128K context and batch 16 on one GB300.

zh.text: Jet-QSparse在Blackwell上结合NVFP4 KV存储、原生FP4键打分与较高精度的稀疏值聚合。128块预算下，已测任务未检测到准确率损失；另一个64块设置中，单张GB300、128K上下文、batch 16的Qwen3.8-27B解码加速1.94倍。

original_abstract.text: Generative recommendation can reproduce a wider beam's ranked output with roughly half the prefix-capacity budget by reallocating retention capacity across semantic-ID positions. We identify a \emph{first-step coverage bottleneck}: across six full-test settings of the TIGER generative recommender spanning three domains and two identifier constructions, every pruned exact top-10 path is first lost at the initial decoding step. An exact-catalog reference isolates search losses and guides a controlled budget intervention. Moving width to the first step raises Search Recall@10 by 0.96--10.90 percentage points at Beam-50's unchanged budget. Across all 77,373 test users with residual-quantized variational autoencoder (RQ-VAE) tokenization, the reallocated schedule reproduces Beam-100's ordered top-10 at nominal budgets of 151 rather than 301, without retraining or changing identifiers or scores. Matched-output timing saves 6.35--6.39\% of decoder latency; profiling identifies the execution costs that limit the translation from reduced search work to runtime savings. Larger-candidate experiments reveal how output size changes retention requirements. These findings make budget placement an actionable serving decision: locate ranking loss, redirect search capacity, and preserve downstream inputs before increasing uniform beam width.
original_abstract.source_title: Where Beam Search Loses Top-Ranked Items:First-Step Coverage in Generative Recommendation

en.text: A controlled TIGER study finds that exact top-10 paths lost by beam search are first pruned at the initial semantic-ID step in six tested settings. Reallocating capacity to that step reproduces Beam-100 output at a nominal budget of 151 rather than 301, while matched-output decoder latency improves by only 6.35–6.39%.

zh.text: 这项TIGER受控实验发现，六个测试设置中被束搜索遗漏的精确top-10路径，首次丢失均发生在语义ID解码第一步。将保留容量前移，可用151而非301的名义预算复现Beam-100输出；相同输出下实际解码延迟改善为6.35%—6.39%。

original_abstract.text: Numerical embeddings map scalar features into vectors before a click-through rate (CTR) backbone combines the fields. To our knowledge, NumEmbBench is the first open benchmark dedicated to comparing numerical embeddings for CTR prediction. We classify 18 configurations into six mechanism-based families and evaluate them through one FuxiCTR interface. After equal-budget validation tuning, we compare frozen configurations on three datasets, nine backbones, and five seeds under a shared train-only z-score protocol. DEER has the best mean rank, but six methods lead at least one dataset--backbone setting. A matched native-scale test changes the winner in 11 of 27 settings, while paired latency measurements show that accuracy and inference cost need not move together. Code and per-seed results: https://github.com/YH-learning/NumEmbBench
original_abstract.source_title: Numerical Embeddings for CTR Prediction: A Taxonomy, Unified Benchmark, and Open-Source FuxiCTR Extension

en.text: NumEmbBench compares 18 numerical-embedding configurations across six mechanism families using a shared FuxiCTR interface, three datasets, nine backbones and five seeds. Native-scale evaluation changes the winner in 11 of 27 settings, highlighting dependence on preprocessing and the need to measure both accuracy and inference latency.

zh.text: NumEmbBench通过统一FuxiCTR接口，在三个数据集、九种骨干和五个随机种子下比较六类机制的18种数值编码配置。改用原始尺度后，27个设置中11个更换最优方法，说明选型需要同时考虑预处理、预测效果和推理延迟。

original_abstract.text: Generative recommendation promises to simplify conventional multi-stage recommender systems by generating item Semantic IDs (SIDs) autoregressively. However, two obstacles limit its effective- ness in industrial settings: interaction-only supervision underuses the semantic knowledge encoded in pretrained language models, while beam-search likelihood ranks token sequences rather than directly estimating item relevance. To address these limitations, we propose HiGenTrans, a three-level framework that introduces LLM knowledge at the input, representation, and decision levels. First, Global Semantic Priming (GSP) adds an LLM-derived user representation to the beginning-of-sequence embedding, provid- ing a semantic prior before SID generation. Second, Hierarchi- cal Representation Transfer (HRT) aligns intermediate LLM representations with depth-matched GenRec layers through mean- centered projections and gated residual connections. Finally, Multi- Signal Decision Calibration (MDC) uses a lightweight mixture- of-experts calibrator to combine semantic relevance, generation confidence, and candidate-set context when reranking beam-search outputs. All semantic features are computed only from the observ- able interaction prefix, preventing target leakage, and can be cached offline. Experiments on three public benchmarks show that HiGen- Trans improves Recall@10 by up to 12.9% and NDCG@10 by up to 33.7% over the strongest baselines. These results demonstrate the value of transferring LLM knowledge at complementary stages of the generative recommendation pipeline.
original_abstract.source_title: HiGenTrans: Hierarchical LLM Knowledge Transfer for Generative Recommendation

en.text: HiGenTrans transfers LLM knowledge into semantic-ID recommendation through a user semantic prior, depth-aligned hidden representations and a lightweight MoE beam-output calibrator. Prefix-only semantic features can be cached offline; three benchmarks show up to 12.9% Recall@10 and 33.7% NDCG@10 improvements over the strongest baselines.

zh.text: HiGenTrans从用户语义先验、按深度对齐的中间表征和轻量MoE候选校准三个层面，将LLM知识迁移到语义ID推荐。仅基于可观测交互前缀的语义特征可离线缓存；三个基准上，相对最强基线的Recall@10与NDCG@10最高分别提升12.9%和33.7%。

original_abstract.text: Semantic IDs (SIDs) have emerged as a promising approach for discriminative recommendation by encoding continuous item rep- resentations into compact discrete identifiers. However, existing SID-based methods face two fundamental limitations: semantic mis- match between content semantics and collaborative preferences, and objective mismatch between SID construction and downstream recommendation optimization. To address these challenges, we propose SIDRec, an end-to-end recommendation-aware SID learn- ing framework that jointly models content and collaborative in- formation while aligning SID construction with recommendation objectives. Specifically, SIDRec introduces a self-updating fusion mechanism that explicitly integrates pretrained content represen- tations with collaborative embeddings initialized from a trained recommendation model, enabling preference-aware semantic mod- eling. Furthermore, SIDRec employs an MMoE-inspired joint opti- mization mechanism with shared experts and task-specific gates, allowing recommendation supervision to directly guide differen- tiable quantization and produce task-adaptive discrete representa- tions. Extensive experiments on three public benchmark datasets demonstrate that SIDRec consistently outperforms all competing methods across both AUC and GAUC, achieving up to 5.15% relative improvements over the strongest baselines. Further ablation stud- ies validate the effectiveness and complementarity of collaborative semantic modeling and end-to-end SID optimization.
original_abstract.source_title: SIDRec: End-to-End Semantic ID Representation and Modeling for Recommendation

en.text: SIDRec jointly learns content and collaborative semantic IDs with recommendation supervision. Self-updating representation fusion and an MMoE-inspired differentiable-quantization objective address semantic and training-objective mismatch; three public datasets show AUC and GAUC improvements, with up to 5.15% relative gains over the strongest baselines.

zh.text: SIDRec将内容与协同信息融合，并用推荐监督端到端学习语义ID。自更新表征融合和受MMoE启发的可微量化联合目标缓解语义与优化目标不一致；三个公开数据集上的AUC和GAUC改善，相对最强基线最高提升5.15%。

original_abstract.text: Relative-position attention mechanisms offer compelling alternatives to RoPE across various transformer architectures, delivering superior performance in domains such as audio. These mechanisms typically modify attention scores by adding content-position or bias-position terms. Unlike RoPE, which encodes position via per-token rotations directly on the queries and keys, relative-position terms generally require pairwise offset-dependent computation or lookups, complicating their integration into fused attention kernels and introducing severe memory, bandwidth, and compute overheads as sequences scale. To address this bottleneck, we propose an exact attention algorithm that incorporates additive relative-position terms into FlashAttention-style tiled computation. Our method (1) uses offset-aware tiling to avoid redundant indexing and memory accesses, (2) computes only the necessary key/query-relation products and reuses them across token pairs in both forward and backward passes, and (3) uses offset-based gradient sharding and aggregation, eliminating atomic contention. We provide a unified, efficient Triton implementation across diverse relative-position attention mechanisms and evaluate it against naive and specialized implementations. For 8K-token sequences, our method speeds up the forward (backward) pass by 1.8-6.4$\times$ (2.0-21$\times$) and reduces peak memory up to 2.9-128$\times$ (1.4-54$\times$) over the strongest baseline for each mechanism, enabling long-context end-to-end transcription that is 1.8$\times$ faster and uses 2.4$\times$ less memory. Our method thus provides a drop-in, hardware-efficient solution for scaling relative-position attention transformers.
original_abstract.source_title: Fast and Exact Relative-Position Attention via Structure-Aware Kernels

en.text: This work integrates additive relative-position attention into exact FlashAttention-style tiling using offset-aware reuse and sharded gradient aggregation. At 8K tokens it reports 1.8–6.4× forward and 2.0–21× backward speedups over the strongest evaluated baseline for each mechanism; a transcription integration is 1.8× faster and uses 2.4× less memory.

zh.text: 该研究将加性相对位置注意力纳入精确的FlashAttention式分块，通过偏移感知复用和梯度分片聚合减少开销。8K token下，相对各机制最强已测基线，前向加速1.8—6.4倍、反向加速2.0—21倍；转录任务集成后速度为1.8倍、内存用量降至约1/2.4。

original_abstract.text: Attention kernels on Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) often underutilize their matrix units (MXUs) because of repeated matrix operand loads, vector-intensive computation, and dependencies that leave MXUs idle. We present FlyWheel, a set of fast TPU kernels for both softmax and linear attention. FlyWheel reformulates softmax and triangular inversion to reduce vector work, while coordinating data layouts to improve matrix operand reuse. It then overlaps independent computation to hide execution latency. We apply these techniques to both softmax attention and Gated DeltaNet on TPU v6e and v7x. FlyWheel speeds up softmax attention by up to $4.14\times$ over the state-of-the-art RPA kernel and $1.80\times$ over Splash Attention, reaching 81% of peak BF16 throughput on v6e. It also speeds up Gated DeltaNet prefill by up to $3.61\times$. Integrated into vLLM serving Qwen3.8-27B, FlyWheel improves prefill throughput by up to $1.56\times$ while maintaining comparable accuracy.
original_abstract.source_title: FlyWheel: Attention Kernels Built for the TPU

en.text: FlyWheel reduces vector work and repeated matrix-operand loads in TPU softmax and linear attention, then overlaps independent computation. Tests on TPU v6e/v7x report up to 4.14× softmax-kernel and 3.61× Gated DeltaNet prefill speedups; Qwen3.8-27B integration improves serving prefill throughput by up to 1.56× with comparable accuracy.

zh.text: FlyWheel减少TPU上softmax与线性注意力的向量运算和矩阵操作数重复加载，并重叠独立计算。TPU v6e/v7x测试报告softmax内核最高加速4.14倍、Gated DeltaNet预填充最高加速3.61倍；集成Qwen3.8-27B后，在准确率相当时服务预填充吞吐最高提升至1.56倍。

original_abstract.text: Generative recommendation retrieves items by autoregressively generating semantic IDs, typically via beam search. On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) enhances training supervision by transferring privileged self-teacher knowledge at student-generated states. However, beam-search retention depends on competition among prefixes: visited states differ in importance, and initially reliable decisions may approach the pruning boundary as training evolves. Moreover, conventional distribution matching couples target-token confidence with preferences among competing continuations, potentially weakening relational supervision when the self-teacher strongly favors the target. To address these challenges, we propose Search-Aware On-Policy Self-Distillation (SA-OPSD), a framework that transfers privileged self-teacher knowledge to the states visited during the student's own beam search. Specifically, we introduce Evolving-Boundary Sampling, which prioritizes search-critical states by considering both current pruning-boundary proximity and initial-reference retention-margin decline under a controlled distillation budget. Furthermore, we develop Confidence-Decoupled Branch Distillation, which separates target-probability calibration from informative sibling relations to better preserve the teacher's preferences among competing branches. Experiments on Industrial, Office, and Instruments demonstrate strong performance for SA-OPSD.
original_abstract.source_title: Search-Aware On-Policy Self-Distillation with Sibling Alignment for Generative Recommendation

en.text: SA-OPSD targets the beam-search states most vulnerable to pruning under a fixed distillation budget. It combines evolving-boundary sampling with confidence-decoupled branch distillation to preserve sibling preferences from a privileged self-teacher, reporting gains on an industrial dataset and two public domains.

zh.text: SA-OPSD在固定蒸馏预算下，优先监督学生束搜索中最容易被裁剪的状态。方法结合演化边界采样和置信度解耦的分支蒸馏，保留特权自教师对兄弟分支的偏好，并在工业数据集及两个公开领域报告提升。

original_abstract.text: The sparse path, comprising sparse operations and collective communication, is a critical component of large-scale recommendation models. However, these operations are often represented as opaque nodes in the training computation graph, hindering whole-graph optimization. We present SparseLift, a low-overhead compiler for the sparse path of large-scale recommendation training. It exposes sparse computation and communication to whole-graph analysis to expand the optimization space and improve training efficiency. By analyzing model structure and runtime information, SparseLift reconstructs opaque nodes as analyzable subgraphs, recovering the resource semantics of sparse computation and communication within the graph. Building on the recovered semantics, we design incremental cost models and a constraint-aware planner to automatically select and organize subgraph optimizations into an execution plan that is reused during subsequent steady-state training. We evaluate SparseLift on an industrial video-platform recommendation task with 100B sparse parameters and the public DLRM benchmark. SparseLift improves steady-state throughput for ordinary industrial training steps by 16.5\% over the native baseline. On DLRM, it achieves $1.60\times$ and $1.26\times$ model-execution speedups over DLRM-Baseline and TorchRec, respectively.
original_abstract.source_title: SparseLift: Automatically Optimizing Opaque Sparse Paths in Industrial-Scale Recommendation Model Training

en.text: SparseLift exposes opaque sparse operations and collective communication as analyzable training subgraphs, then uses incremental cost models and a constraint-aware planner to reuse optimized execution plans. It reports 16.5% higher ordinary steady-state throughput on a 100B-sparse-parameter industrial recommender and 1.60×/1.26× model-execution speedups over DLRM-Baseline/TorchRec.

zh.text: SparseLift将不透明的稀疏算子与集合通信展开为可分析子图，用增量成本模型和约束规划器生成可复用的训练执行计划。在1000亿稀疏参数的工业推荐模型上，普通稳态训练步吞吐提升16.5%；DLRM模型执行速度分别为DLRM-Baseline和TorchRec的1.60倍、1.26倍。

original_abstract.text: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture has been widely adopted in large language models (LLMs) since it reduces the computational cost through sparse expert activation. However, the massive parameter scale of MoE models hinders their deployment on resource-constrained edge devices. Although existing mixed-precision quantization reduces the model size, they are inherently static, fixing the bit-width of each expert across decoding steps. Such static schemes yield suboptimal performance as they overlook the dynamic variation in expert importance during decoding. Furthermore, they fail to adapt to the dynamic latency constraint driven by the fluctuating system utilization. To address these challenges, we propose MatMoE, a dynamic mixed-precision quantization framework for efficient MoE inference. MatMoE features: (1) a Matryoshka MoE PTQ algorithm that enables experts to operate flexibly at multiple precisions within a stringent memory budget; (2) a floor-and-compensation quantization method that eliminates redundant memory accesses in the Matryoshka representation; and (3) a dynamic bit-width allocation strategy that determines the precision for each expert based on their routing scores to satisfy the dynamic latency requirement. We implement our MatMoE system atop llama.cpp for both CPU and GPU platforms. Extensive evaluations across three modern MoE models and challenging benchmarks demonstrate that MatMoE achieves $4.0\% \sim 18.3\%$ higher accuracy than state-of-the-art static mixed-precision method. Compared to llama.cpp, MatMoE delivers $1.3\times \sim 3.7\times$ speedup on Raspberry Pi 5, and $1.2\times \sim 1.3\times$ speedup on NVIDIA RTX 4090 and Jetson AGX Orin.
original_abstract.source_title: MatMoE: Matryoshka Mixture-of-Experts with Dynamic Mixed-Precision Quantization for Efficient Inference

en.text: MatMoE combines nested multi-precision expert representations, floor-and-compensation quantization and routing-aware dynamic bit allocation for changing latency budgets. Implemented in llama.cpp, it reports 1.3–3.7× speedups on Raspberry Pi 5 and 1.2–1.3× on RTX 4090 and Jetson AGX Orin, alongside accuracy gains over the tested static mixed-precision method.

zh.text: MatMoE结合嵌套多精度专家表示、基础值与补偿量化，以及依据路由分数的动态比特分配，适配变化的延迟预算。基于llama.cpp的实现报告在树莓派5上加速1.3—3.7倍，在RTX 4090和Jetson AGX Orin上加速1.2—1.3倍，并较所测静态混合精度方法改善准确率。

original_abstract.text: Delta-rule linear attention underlies language models such as Kimi Linear and Qwen3-Next. Chunkwise implementations expose matrix parallelism, but their backward passes compute unnecessary auxiliary adjoints. We present ReWY, an algebraic reformulation that reduces this work before optimizing accelerator execution. Differentiating the chunk correction as one triangular residual system eliminates the inverse adjoint and reduces seven local WY matrix products to three. Two complementary transformations expose further reuse: centered matrix contractions replace pairwise vector-gate processing, and scalar-gate reductions reuse key-gradient products instead of forming a key Gram matrix. These identities simplify backward computation for DeltaNet, GDN, KDA, and GDN2 while preserving the recurrence and gradients in exact arithmetic, without changing the architecture or training objective. We implement the reduced graph on GPUs and Ascend NPUs. Under matched recomputation and full-saving policies, precision-qualified six-shape comparisons with frozen FLA references yield 1.15-1.81$\times$ geometric-mean complete low-level backward speedups on NVIDIA GPUs. All four operators achieve 1.18-1.70$\times$ on H100 and H200 while retaining original FP32 working matrices. A separate public-autograd evaluation on Ascend 950DT, including gradient conversions, yields 1.09-2.89$\times$ under available matched policies. Paired ablations establish further ReWY gains after optimizing the complementary contractions. Complete-gradient checks validate the recorded operator cases; supplementary full-model backward measurements assess integration into community FLA models and a GDN2 layer port. Code and reproduction materials: https://github.com/flashserve/ReWY.
original_abstract.source_title: ReWY: Faster Backpropagation for Delta-Rule Attention - From 7 to 3 Matrix Multiplications

en.text: ReWY algebraically simplifies the backward pass of DeltaNet, GDN, KDA and GDN2, reducing seven local WY matrix products to three while preserving exact-arithmetic gradients. GPU and Ascend implementations exploit further contraction reuse; matched-policy GPU tests report 1.15–1.81× geometric-mean low-level backward speedups.

zh.text: ReWY以代数重构简化DeltaNet、GDN、KDA和GDN2反向传播，将七次局部WY矩阵乘法减少到三次，并保持精确算术下梯度一致。GPU和昇腾实现进一步复用张量收缩；匹配存储与重计算策略的GPU测试中，底层完整反向的几何平均加速为1.15—1.81倍。

original_abstract.text: Scaling laws predict the outcome of large, expensive training runs by extrapolating trends from smaller, cheaper runs. On downstream accuracy evaluations, these predictions fail when the weaker models produced by the cheaper runs score near zero accuracy, because these scores give no trend to extrapolate to larger scales. We introduce hinted scaling laws, which use privileged information to turn a benchmark into a continuum of easier versions so that even the small models score above zero. We find that accuracy rises smoothly and predictably with the hint level, enabling new types of scaling laws that operate below the noise threshold. On the Delphi pretraining ladder, a hinted scaling law fit on models trained with at most $10^{20}$ FLOPs forecasts the GSM8K accuracy of a $10^{23}$ FLOP model (25.9%) to within 3 percentage points; a standard scaling law under-forecasts it by 13 percentage points when fit on the same models and by 12 even with models up to $10^{22}$ FLOPs in the fit. Across both this pretraining ladder and a collection of post-trained model families, hinted scaling laws reduce the median forecasting error on GSM8K, AIME and HLE from 21 percentage points to 4.3. Hinting also reduces the number of test examples needed to tell whether one model is better than another by widening the accuracy gaps between models while approximately preserving their order: a single hinted rollout per problem ranks nearly indistinguishable models as accurately as five unhinted rollouts. Our results suggest that hinting is a general primitive for improving the accuracy and cost of downstream scaling laws and other prediction tasks in model development.
original_abstract.source_title: Hinted Scaling Laws

en.text: Hinted Scaling Laws uses privileged hints to make difficult evaluations informative for small models, then extrapolates performance across hint levels and compute scales. On pretraining and post-training model families, the reported median forecast error on GSM8K, AIME and HLE falls from 21 to 4.3 percentage points, offering a model-development tool rather than a validated recommendation scaling law.

zh.text: Hinted Scaling Laws借助特权提示，使小模型在困难评测上得到可用信号，再沿提示程度与训练规模外推性能。在预训练及后训练模型族上，GSM8K、AIME和HLE的预测误差中位数从21降到4.3个百分点；其价值在模型开发方法，尚非已验证的推荐扩展规律。

original_abstract.text: Residual connections give each Transformer block access to all earlier layers only through one fixed sum, broadcast to all of the block's inputs. This broadcast bottleneck imposes three constraints: the query, key, value and residual inputs of a block, which we call its roles, read the same vector; all hidden dimensions within a role share one set of weights over earlier layers; and every earlier layer has the same fixed weight for every token. We propose the Multi-Role Multi-Group Mixing Residual (M3), which removes all three: every role, and every group of hidden dimensions within a role, reads its own token-dependent mixture of all earlier layers. M3 starts as an exact residual connection and adds as little as 1.4% parameters and 1.8% FLOPs. From 100M to 1.4B parameters, M3Former outperforms the Transformer and coarse-grained cross-layer connections at every size, matching a Transformer 1.19-1.34x the size of the one it modifies, trained with 1.4-1.8x the compute. Relaxing only some of the constraints recovers only part of this gain. M3Former also improves sparse mixture-of-experts models of up to 4.6B parameters and trains more stably in deeper networks. Code: https://github.com/Kingchet10/m3former
original_abstract.source_title: M3Former: Fine-Grained Cross-Layer Mixing for Transformers

en.text: M3Former lets query, key, value and residual roles read separate token-dependent mixtures of earlier layers, further separating groups of hidden dimensions. It initializes as an exact residual connection and can add only 1.4% parameters and 1.8% FLOPs; experiments from 100M to 1.4B parameters report gains over conventional and coarser cross-layer connections, with extensions to sparse MoE.

zh.text: M3Former让查询、键、值及残差分别读取随token变化的历史层混合，并进一步按隐藏维度分组。模块初始化为精确残差连接，最低只增加1.4%参数和1.8% FLOPs；1亿至14亿参数实验显示优于常规与粗粒度跨层连接，并扩展验证到稀疏MoE。

original_abstract.text: Reasoning-augmented recommender systems (RecSys) enhance user preference modeling by generating reasoning trajectories over historical interactions before making recommendations. Knowledge distillation provides a practical paradigm for transferring such reasoning capabilities from powerful large language models to lightweight RecSys. However, existing methods typically rely on a single fixed teacher, remain constrained by the teacher knowledge ceiling, and indiscriminately distill teacher-generated trajectories without assessing their actual utility for downstream recommendation. To address these limitations, we propose MUSE (Multi-Teacher Utility-guided Selection with Self-Exploration), an adaptive reasoning distillation framework that jointly improves reasoning generation and reasoning utilization. MUSE first constructs a diverse reasoning pool using multiple teacher LLMs and progressively augments it via student self-exploration, enabling the student to leverage the strengths of different teachers and gradually explore reasoning strategies beyond teacher imitation. We then develop Rank-Gain Utility Assessment (RGUA), which evaluates each candidate according to the normalized full-catalog rank improvement of the ground-truth item and identifies the most and least recommendation-beneficial trajectories. Based on these utility-aware trajectory pairs, we introduce dual-level contrastive learning objectives that guide the student generator to prefer beneficial reasoning while training the recommendation encoder to more effectively exploit recommendation-relevant preference evidence. Extensive experiments on three real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed framework.
original_abstract.source_title: Multi-Teacher Reasoning Distillation for LLM Recommendation with Self-Exploration

en.text: MUSE combines reasoning from multiple teachers with student self-exploration and scores trajectories by full-catalog rank improvement. Dual-level contrastive objectives teach the generator to prefer useful reasoning and the recommendation encoder to exploit it; experiments cover three datasets.

zh.text: MUSE结合多教师推理和学生自探索，以目标物品在全目录中的排名改善衡量推理轨迹价值。双层对比目标分别训练生成器选择有用推理、推荐编码器利用偏好证据，并在三个数据集上验证。

original_abstract.text: Learned sparse attention, used in production models such as DeepSeek-V4 and GLM-5, lets each query attend to only k keys chosen by a lightweight indexer, but the indexer still scores every key in the prefix. At one million tokens, this selection takes more than half of prefill time. Two-stage selection over contiguous blocks, as in HiSA, reduces this cost, but its recall declines as context grows at a fixed candidate budget. We present AttentionIndex, which routes each query over an inverted-file index that groups indexer keys by similarity and refines the candidates with the native indexer score. AttentionIndex builds the index during prefill, making new keys searchable immediately, reusing previous clustering to keep maintenance cheap, and exposing each query only to clusters built from its own prefix. On GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek-V4-Flash at one million tokens, AttentionIndex delivers 1.3-1.8 times the prefill throughput of exhaustive selection, and at throughput within 5% of HiSA, it recovers 17.0 and 10.0 percentage points more of the exhaustive top-k, respectively. AttentionIndex also improves accuracy on long-context benchmarks by up to 18.4 percentage points over HiSA at the same candidate budget.
original_abstract.source_title: AttentionIndex: Accelerating Learned Sparse Attention with a Causal Inverted-File Index

en.text: AttentionIndex uses a causal inverted-file index to avoid scoring every key in learned sparse attention. At one million tokens on GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek-V4-Flash, prefill throughput is 1.3–1.8× exhaustive selection; at throughput within 5% of HiSA it recovers 17 and 10 percentage points more of exhaustive top-k respectively.

zh.text: AttentionIndex以因果倒排索引替代学习式稀疏注意力对全部历史键的逐一打分。在百万token的GLM-5.3与DeepSeek-V4-Flash测试中，预填充吞吐为穷举选择的1.3—1.8倍；吞吐与HiSA相差不超过5%时，分别多找回17和10个百分点的穷举top-k结果。

original_abstract.text: Recommendation models consume increasingly long, attribute-rich user histories, making small continuous updates and repeated large reads a central storage asymmetry. We present USDB, ByteDance's unified sequence storage practice for streaming and batch workloads. CascadeLSM time-based compaction stages materialize application-specific histories; differentiated replicas share persistent files; partial dumps reconstruct inference inputs from captured recent state and versioned history; and a hybrid columnar format accelerates projected reads. These designs reuse maintenance results across ingestion, inference, and training. Production migration records show 85.8% lower mean write latency, while normalized deployment accounting shows 42.1% lower infrastructure cost. Controlled comparisons with an Optimized RocksDB sequence baseline show faster long-history reads across projections and client loads. Aggregation pushdown sustains 8.5x the throughput of ordinary reads under a constrained receive budget. Production reconstruction and direct-file training results demonstrate how shared sequence maintenance supports fresh serving and repeated historical access.
original_abstract.source_title: USDB: Scaling Storage for Next-Generation Recommender Systems at ByteDance

en.text: USDB addresses the mismatch between small streaming updates and repeated long-history reads in recommendation storage. CascadeLSM compaction, shared-file replicas, partial dumps and a hybrid columnar format reuse maintenance work across ingestion, serving and training; production records report 85.8% lower mean write latency and normalized accounting reports 42.1% lower infrastructure cost.

zh.text: USDB针对推荐存储中小规模持续写入与长历史反复读取的不对称，结合CascadeLSM分层压缩、共享文件副本、局部转储和混合列式格式，在写入、推理及训练间复用维护结果。生产迁移记录显示平均写延迟降低85.8%，归一化部署核算显示基础设施成本降低42.1%。

original_abstract.text: Generative recommendation has been widely adopted in large-scale industrial recommendation systems, where multimodal item embeddings are quantized into offline semantic identifiers (SIDs) and items are retrieved by autoregressively generating their SIDs. However, conventional SID construction often underrepresents item utility reflected in post-exposure behaviors such as shares, long views, and video completion, making semantically similar items with different utility insufficiently distinguishable while struggling to accommodate rapidly changing utility signals. Moreover, generation likelihood may be misaligned with downstream utility, causing high-utility candidates to be prematurely pruned during beam search before post-generation reranking or training-time reward alignment can effectively compensate. To address these limitations, we propose UAGR, which aligns both SID construction and decoding with downstream multi-objective utility. Our Utility-Enriched Semantic Codes preserve the original semantic information while incorporating item-level utility without increasing SID length or vocabulary size, supporting incremental utility updates with no additional tokenization or sequence-decoding cost. Meanwhile, our Utility-Guided Decoding estimates candidate utility by combining predictions of multiple post-exposure outcomes and incorporates these estimates into beam scoring, reducing the risk of prematurely pruning high-utility paths while enabling flexible utility control without interfering with generative backbone training. Extensive offline experiments and online A/B tests under real-world traffic demonstrate the effectiveness and deployability of UAGR, which has been fully deployed on Kuaishou and increases video watch time by 0.206\% online.
original_abstract.source_title: Utility-Aware Generative Recommendation: Utility-Enriched Semantic Codes and Utility-Guided Decoding

en.text: UAGR incorporates post-exposure utility into semantic codes and beam scoring without increasing semantic-ID length or vocabulary size. Incremental utility updates and utility-guided decoding aim to retain valuable candidates early; the authors report full Kuaishou deployment and a 0.206% online watch-time increase.

zh.text: UAGR把曝光后行为效用融入语义编码与束搜索打分，同时保持语义ID长度和词表规模不变。增量效用更新与效用引导解码帮助提前保留高价值候选；作者报告已在快手全量部署，线上观看时长提升0.206%。

original_abstract.text: Large language model (LLM) embeddings have been increasingly adopted in sequential recommendation to encode static item attributes and alleviate the limitations of item ID embeddings under sparse interactions. However, these embeddings typically capture only static content similarity while neglecting sequential transitions, and since their adaptation quality relies on sparse per-item updates or global geometric calibration, existing methods still struggle to explicitly transfer preceding interaction contexts from frequent to long-tail items under unevenly distributed behavioral evidence, limiting recommendation effectiveness across the catalog. To address this challenge, we propose PACERec, an ID-free progressive adaptation framework that incorporates preceding interaction contexts into semantic representation adaptation by learning a shared velocity field from items with sufficient interactions via frequency-weighted flow matching. In this way, PACERec progressively guides static LLM embeddings toward collaborative behavioral targets while preserving original item semantics, overcoming sparse per-item updates to effectively generalize sequential transition patterns to long-tail items for both user modeling and candidate scoring. Extensive experiments on three real-world datasets across three sequential backbones demonstrate the superiority of our method over competitive baselines in both overall and long-tail recommendation.
original_abstract.source_title: PACERec: Progressive Adaptation of LLM Item Embeddings with Collaborative Evidence for Recommendation

en.text: PACERec uses frequency-weighted flow matching to adapt static LLM item embeddings toward collaborative behavioral targets. A shared velocity field transfers preceding-interaction patterns from frequent to long-tail items, with improvements reported across three datasets and three sequential backbones.

zh.text: PACERec通过频次加权的流匹配，将静态LLM物品向量逐步适配到协同行为目标。共享速度场把高频物品的前序交互规律迁移给长尾物品，作者在三个数据集、三种序列骨干上报告效果提升。

original_abstract.text:
Large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models are promising for local inference because sparse routing allows the routed-expert pool to reside on SSD while DRAM caches recently used experts. However, under practical DRAM cache capacities, substantial SSD I/O remains on the critical path despite I/O-computation overlap. Token-level dynamic expert precision offers a natural way to reduce this data demand by allocating bits according to expert importance and quantization sensitivity. Nevertheless, treating each bit-width of the same expert as an independent object prevents cross-precision cache reuse, causing overlapping data to be fetched repeatedly.
  The key insight is that precision should instead denote the refinement depth of one shared expert state. Based on this insight, we present PagedMoE, which stores each expert once using a prefix-compatible tree codebook and bitplane layout. Lower-precision representations are valid prefixes of higher-precision ones, allowing cached data to be reused or extended by fetching only missing bitplanes. PagedMoE selects the required prefix length before I/O using current routing weights and offline expert-specific error profiles, and directly executes cached 1-8-bit prefixes without materializing full-precision experts.
  At an average routed-expert precision of 2.5 bits, PagedMoE achieves quality close to GPTQ-INT4 on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B and to MXFP4 on most evaluated GLM5.2 tasks. With a 24 GiB expert cache, it reaches 8.89 tokens/s on Qwen3.5, 1.33x the throughput of the same dynamic requests using independent precision objects and 1.56x that of uniform 4-bit execution.
original_abstract.source_title: PagedMoE: Cross-Precision Expert Caching for Token-Level Dynamic Precision in SSD-Resident MoE Inference

en.text: PagedMoE stores each SSD-resident expert in a prefix-compatible codebook and bitplane layout so cached low-bit representations can be extended rather than refetched. At 2.5-bit average routed-expert precision and a 24 GiB expert cache, Qwen3.5 reaches 8.89 tokens/s, 1.33× independent-precision objects and 1.56× uniform 4-bit execution, with quality close to GPTQ-INT4.

zh.text: PagedMoE使用前缀兼容码本与位平面布局存储SSD上的专家，使缓存的低比特表示可增量扩展而无需重复读取。在路由专家平均2.5比特、专家缓存24 GiB时，Qwen3.5达到8.89 token/s，为独立精度对象方案的1.33倍、统一4比特执行的1.56倍，质量接近GPTQ-INT4。

original_abstract.text: Long-context LLM inference is costly because attention repeatedly reads a growing key-value (KV) history. We introduce Chunk-Indexed Sparse Attention (CISA), which retrofits pretrained dense attention models without gradient updates. CISA selects fixed-size KV chunks using compact summaries of existing keys, avoiding token-level indexing and a separate full-length index cache. It uses one indexing query per KV group and shares selected chunks across queries in that group. During prefill, QShare reuses selections across adjacent queries to reduce indexing cost and improve KV reuse and GPU utilization. We evaluate CISA on NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano and Ultra, and Inkling-Small. In one-layer BF16 benchmarks at batch size 32 using Ultra's per-device attention dimensions, core attention is 11.7x faster for prefill queries near the end of a 1M-token prompt and 13.0x faster during decode. Including chunk scoring, selection, and all other measured GPU work, speedups are 8.6x and 3.0x. On Ultra NVFP4 with a 4,096-chunk budget, aggregate scores stay within 1.5 percentage points of dense attention on MRCR, LongBench v2, and GraphWalks. RULER sweeps on Nano and Ultra BF16 up to one million tokens show scores within 2.05 percentage points of dense attention with 8-16x fewer KV reads. Serving million-token prompts with 32 concurrent requests and 4K output tokens per request, CISA achieves 2.29x the end-to-end throughput of dense attention using Nemotron 3 Ultra NVFP4 on four NVIDIA B300 GPUs. Selecting fewer chunks increases throughput to 2.61x; in separate GraphWalks evaluations, the smaller budget widens the aggregate score gap from 1.49 to 3.59 percentage points. These results expose a practical quality-speed tradeoff without sparse training.
original_abstract.source_title: CISA: Retrofitting Dense Attention Models with Chunk-Indexed Sparse Attention

en.text: CISA retrofits dense attention without gradient updates by selecting fixed-size KV chunks using compact key summaries and sharing selections across queries. A four-B300 Nemotron 3 Ultra NVFP4 serving test reports 2.29× end-to-end throughput; tighter chunk budgets increase speed while widening quality gaps.

zh.text: CISA通过紧凑键摘要选择固定大小的KV块，并跨查询复用选择结果，无需梯度更新即可改造稠密注意力。四张B300上的Nemotron 3 Ultra NVFP4服务测试报告端到端吞吐为稠密版本的2.29倍；进一步缩减块预算可提高速度，但质量差距也会扩大。

original_abstract.text: Generative recommendation generates the semantic ID (SID) of the next item from a user's interaction history. Existing training objectives mainly supervise target SID tokens, while on-policy distillation (OPD) provides denser supervision through a teacher's probability distribution over all tokens for more effective and efficient training. However, OPD can aggravate popularity bias: teacher feedback favors popular-item tokens, transferring this preference to the student, while student rollout favors popular items, leaving unpopular-item SID paths rarely generated and supervised. These two sources of bias reinforce each other and reduce recommendation diversity. We propose HERO, a diversity-aware OPD framework. Heterogeneous teacher distillation trains two teachers specializing in popular and unpopular items and routes each training sample to the teacher matching the popularity group of its ground-truth item. The student learns from the routed teacher's probability distribution along its own generated SIDs. Diversity-aware item rollout incorporates ground-truth SIDs of unpopular items into training, covering SID paths that the student rarely generates. Only the student is used for inference. Offline experiments on an industrial dataset and three public datasets further demonstrate its effectiveness, diversity, and robustness. Moreover, we deploy HERO in the "Guess What You Like" module on the 1688 homepage, where a 15-day online A/B test shows a 3.412% increase in gross merchandise value (GMV).
original_abstract.source_title: Diverse-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Generative Recommendation

en.text: HERO routes popular and long-tail training examples to specialized teachers and supplements rare student-generated semantic-ID paths. Only the student serves inference; the authors report offline improvements and a 3.412% GMV increase in a 15-day 1688 A/B test.

zh.text: HERO将热门和长尾样本分别交给专长不同的教师蒸馏，并补充学生较少生成的长尾语义ID路径。推理仅使用学生模型；作者报告离线效果改善，以及1688上15天A/B实验中GMV提升3.412%。
